headline: Chelsea hold on at Stamford Bridge as Jackson's 79th-minute winner edges West Ham
paragraphs: Chelsea beat West Ham 2-1 at Stamford Bridge in a simulated Premier League fixture, with Nicolas Jackson scoring the winner in the 79th minute, assisted by Enzo Fernández. Mohammed Kudus had given West Ham the lead in the 11th minute, assisted by Emerson, after a 0.177 xG finish, before Fernández equalised in the 36th minute (xG 0.158), set up by Jackson. The xG gap was decisive: Chelsea finished on 3.51 xG from 19 shots (10 on target) against West Ham's 1.87 xG from 7 shots (3 on target).

Chelsea controlled the territory and the chance quality. They held 51% possession, a field tilt of 58 against West Ham's 42, and a control rating of 62 to 56. Seven big chances were logged in total, four of them for Chelsea (Jackson at 6 and 19 minutes, Madueke at 13 and 82, Fernández at 72), and West Ham's two were both by Lucas Paquetá, at 26 minutes (0.341 xG) and 30 minutes (0.718 xG), which came in the spell that produced West Ham's momentum swing at 29 minutes. Chelsea's own swing came at 48 minutes. Pass accuracy was level at 80% for both sides.

Discipline became a talking point. Malo Gusto was cards-shown four times for Chelsea (38, 41, 56 and 74 minutes), while Maximilian Kilman was booked for West Ham at 79 minutes, the same minute Jackson scored. Chaos was rated 33 with a tempo of 4.7 passes per minute. Jackson finished with 1.42 xG, 4 duels won and 87% pass accuracy, and Fernández with 0.79 xG, 8 duels won and 90% pass accuracy. Emerson recorded 13 duels won for West Ham at 67% pass accuracy.
